proposed_english: the Gate of those of the Darkness
rationale: ⲡⲣ̄ⲟ = ⲣⲟ 'mouth, door, gate'; ⲛⲁⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ = 'those belonging to the darkness' (genitive of belonging). Technical Manichaean term for the chief opening/portal of the dark realm; this kephalaion treats its epistemic capacities and limits.
Lyc reflex of Greek loanword ϩⲟⲙⲓⲗⲓⲁ < ὁμιλία. Used here twice (lines 1, 9) for the inner communion of speech that the gate of darkness lacks despite its external perception.
From ⲥⲧⲟⲓ 'smell, odor.' In correspondential register, the 'scent of the (five) worlds' parallels other sensory-domain markers in Manichaean cosmology (taste, sound, color).

Despite formal similarity to ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four,' the Manichaean Five Worlds of Darkness (smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness) provides overwhelming context. Possibly a Lyc orthographic variant for ⲡϯⲟⲩ. Flag for human review.
Greek loanwords σκέψις 'examination' and σκέπτομαι 'examine' — used together in lines 4-5 for the deliberative examination the dark powers undertake among themselves.
Lyc reflex of Sahidic ϩⲣⲟⲩⲙⲡⲉ 'thunder.' The gate of darkness, when speaking, is likened to thunder in the clouds — a theophanic-terror image.
Lyc reflex of ⲃⲉⲛⲓⲡⲉ 'iron.' Cosmological-correspondential register: the gate of darkness manifests as a great iron sphere — iron IS the substance of the dark realm.

proposed_english: uncertain — possibly 'constraint' (= ἀνάγκη) or 'realm/array' of the demons
rationale: Etymology unclear. Tentative options: (a) ἀνάγκη 'necessity, constraint'; (b) corrupt form of ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ; (c) abstract from ⲱϫⲛ 'fail.' Context: 'these evil signs exist in the X of the demons.' Flag for review.
Lyc reflex of ϩⲁⲗⲏⲧ 'bird, fowl.' The simile in line 25 compares dispersed/falling figures to scattered birds.
